To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a bounded perturbation α′ of a one-parameter automorphism group α of a von Neummann algebra can be implemented in exactly one way by a strongly continuous unitary group with self- adjoint generator.
a bounded perturbation can be implemented by the same Hamiltonian, and that the corresponding perturbation of the Hamiltonian is of the form H′=VHV −1 + h, whereV is unitary.

bounded perturbations of one-parameter automorphism group of a von Neuman algebra are in bijective correspondence with bounded perturbations (in the sense of bounded perturbation of the Hamiltonians) of one-parameter groups of unitary operators that implement the automorphism group, and that the latter are in bijective correspondences with bounded perturbatons of the generators (Hamiltonians) of such one-parameter groups of implementing unitaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem: given a one-parameter automorphism groupα of a von Neuman algebraM, what are the one-parameter automorphism subgroupsα′ ofM which can be realized as bounded perturbations of α.
the following problem: given two one-parameter automorphism α and α′ ofM, is it true that α′ can be written as a bounded perturbation α′=α+δ of α, where δ is a derivation ofM?
the study of the bounded perturbation theory for von Neumann algebras.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bounded perturbative dynamics is completely characterized by a pair of self-adjoint operators (H,h)∈M2.
a bounded perturbation is a perturbation by a unitary and a bounded operator.
the bounded perturbative dynamics of a von Neumann algebraM is completely determined by the Hamiltonians ofM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bounded perturbative dynamics is the same as the one of the corresponding Hamiltonian.
the bounded perturbatios of the dynamics of the system are the same as the bounded perturbatiions of the Hamiltonian of the system.
the bounded perturbatons of a dynamics α are exactly the ones of the formα′t=UαtU−1, where U is a unitary inM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bounded perturbative dynamics of a von Neumman algebra is governed by the bounded perturbational dynamics of its self-adjoint elements.
bounded perturbations of a one-parameter automorphism group α of a von Neumman algebraM can be described as those automorphism groups of the form α′=AdVαAdV−1, where V is a unitary operator ofM.
the perturbation theory of one-parameter automorphism group of von Neumann algebras is very similar to the corresponding perturbation theory in the context of C*-algebras.
